deep.reconstruction:
Context: genus 3 (p=3), i.e. a plane quartic in Riemann's form sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0 (eq. (9) of the manuscript). Here x,y,z,xi,eta,zeta are linear forms tied by three linear relations: x+y+z+xi+eta+zeta=0 and two of the type a x+b y+c z+a' xi+b' eta+c' zeta=0 with aa'=bb'=cc'. The six forms are bitangents, and the 'Abelian functions' sqrt(linear form) carry the odd theta characteristics. On the next page the characteristics are fixed: (sqrt x)=(n+p), (sqrt y)=(n+q), (sqrt z)=(n+r), (sqrt xi)=(n+q+r), (sqrt eta)=(n+r+p), (sqrt zeta)=(n+p+q). The 16 further bitangents of (16) are sqrt(x+y+z)=(d), sqrt(x+eta+zeta)=(p+d), ..., and the analogous ones for e, f, g. A 'group' (p) is the set of 6 pairs of odd characteristics whose sums equal p; in modern terms it is a Steiner complex of 12 bitangents.

Top of page (end of a previous argument). It treats triples such as (sqrt x)+(sqrt xi)+(p) [reading uncertain]. The conclusion is that none of the 16 functions of (16) can occur in any of the three groups (sqrt(x eta))=(sqrt(y xi)) [group r], (sqrt(x zeta))=(sqrt(z xi)) [group q] and (sqrt(y zeta))=(sqrt(z eta)) [group p].

Counting. The 16 characteristics from (16) are therefore all the odd ('Abelian') characteristics not in the group (sqrt(x xi)) = (p+q+r). That group holds 12 = 6 pairs. Three pairs are already known: (x,xi), (y,eta), (z,zeta). So 6 functions are missing, and finding them completes all 28 = 16 + 12.

Method (self-similarity of the normal form). Put t=x+y+z (so (sqrt t)=(d)) and u = xi+eta+z. The manuscript reads u=xi+eta+zeta, but it must be xi+eta+z; see corrections. Then (sqrt u)=(r+d).

Eq. (20): sqrt(tu) = sqrt(x eta) + sqrt(y xi), 'easily obtained from (16)'. My check: square both sides and use the squared quartic xi x + y eta + 2 sqrt(x y xi eta) = z zeta. Then (20) is equivalent, up to the sign of the square root, to tu + z zeta = x eta + y xi + x xi + y eta. That identity is t u - (x+y)(xi+eta) = z(x+y+z+xi+eta) = -z zeta, which holds by the relation x+y+z+xi+eta+zeta=0.

So (t,x,y,u,eta,xi) satisfy an equation of the same shape as (x,y,z,xi,eta,zeta), and the whole previous investigation can be repeated with this substitution.

Eq. (21): the analogue of the first linear relation is t-x-y-u+eta+xi=0. With t=x+y+z and u=xi+eta+z it is identically 0. Its coefficient products are 1*(-1) = (-1)*1 = (-1)*1 = -1, so it is of type (22).

Eq. (22): there are three more relations a t+b x+c y+a' u+b' eta+c' xi=0 with aa'=bb'=cc'.

Eq. (23): the old groups (p+q+r),(p),(q),(r) are replaced by
- (sqrt tu)=(sqrt x eta)=(sqrt y xi) = (r): d+(r+d) = r; (n+p)+(n+r+p) = r; (n+q)+(n+q+r) = r.
- (sqrt x xi)=(sqrt y eta)=(sqrt z zeta) = (p+q+r).
- (sqrt t xi)=(sqrt u y) = (n+d+q+r).
- (sqrt t eta)=(sqrt u x) = (n+d+p+r).

The group (r) contains exactly the 6 pairs (n+p)+(n+r+p), (n+q)+(n+r+q), (d)+(r+d), (e)+(r+e), (f)+(r+f), (g)+(r+g). That is: (x,eta), (y,xi), (t,u), and the e-, f-, g-pairs sqrt(alpha x+beta y+gamma z) with sqrt(xi/alpha+eta/beta+gamma z), etc.

The page breaks off with a cancelled attempt to list pairs in the 3rd and 4th groups, e.g. (n+d+q+r) as sqrt(t-x-y) = sqrt z, with factor (-u+eta+xi) = -z. The purpose is to obtain the 6 missing bitangents of the Steiner complex (p+q+r) as images of known ones under the substitution.
errors: Transcribed definition u = xi+eta+zeta is inconsistent with the rest of the page. With it, (21) would reduce to z - zeta = 0, which is false, and (sqrt tu) would not equal (r). It must read u = xi+eta+z, which makes (21) an identity and gives (sqrt u)=(r+d). This is likely a transcription error rather than Riemann's.

(20) holds only up to the sign convention of the square roots: the identity forces sqrt(tu) = ±(sqrt(x eta) - sqrt(y xi)) relative to the sign choice in the quartic sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0. This is harmless, since signs of radicals are conventional.

In (23), line 2 lists (sqrt x xi)=(sqrt y eta)=(sqrt z zeta). The exact image of old group (p) under the substitution is (sqrt x xi)=(sqrt y eta); sqrt(z zeta) is a further (correct) member of the same group, so this is not an error.
Cancelled first list (r)=(d)+(r+d)=... ending '= g' was replaced by a correct list; the final list is correct.

results.what: 28 bitangents of the quartic sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0 split as 16 + 12, where the 12 form the 'group' (Steiner complex) with characteristic p+q+r; 6 are still missing
results.modern_name: Steiner complexes of bitangents / odd theta characteristics of genus 3; 28 = 16 + 12 decomposition
results.usually_credited_to: Steiner (1855), Hesse (1855); theta-characteristic version Riemann (lectures) and H. Weber (1876)

results.what: Substitution (x,y,z,xi,eta,zeta) -> (t,x,y,u,eta,xi) with t=x+y+z, u=xi+eta+z gives a new representation sqrt(tu)=sqrt(x eta)+sqrt(y xi) of the same quartic in Riemann normal form, with induced linear relations (21),(22)
results.modern_name: Change of Riemann normal form / Aronhold-type symmetry acting on bitangent configuration
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann ('Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen fuer den Fall p=3', Werke 1876, ed. Weber); Weber, Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen vom Geschlecht 3 (1876)

results.what: Characteristics of the products of the new pairs: (sqrt tu)=(r), (sqrt t xi)=(sqrt uy)=(n+d+q+r), (sqrt t eta)=(sqrt ux)=(n+d+p+r); group (r) has the 6 pairs listed
results.modern_name: Addition of theta characteristics; syzygetic/azygetic pair structure in Steiner complexes
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann/Weber; later Frobenius (1880s) for systematic theory

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of Riemann's known genus-3 theory: the quartic sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0 and the bitangent/characteristic bookkeeping, published posthumously via Weber (Werke 1876; Weber's 1876 book). The page is a working draft of that material; the 'H.W.' on the next page may indicate Weber's hand or annotation. The content is correct and routine within that theory.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,xi,eta=symbols('x y z xi eta'); zeta=-(x+y+z+xi+eta); t=x+y+z; u=xi+eta+z; expand(t*u + z*zeta - (x*eta + y*xi + x*xi + y*eta)) == 0
checkable.asserts: Given x+y+z+xi+eta+zeta=0 and u=xi+eta+z, (20) is consistent with the quartic: tu - x eta - y xi = -(z zeta - x xi - y eta), i.e. sqrt(tu) = ±(sqrt(x eta) - sqrt(y xi)) whenever sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,xi,eta=symbols('x y z xi eta'); t=x+y+z; u=xi+eta+z; expand(t-x-y-u+eta+xi) == 0
checkable.asserts: Relation (21) holds identically with u = xi+eta+z.

transcription_corrections: 'u = xi+eta+zeta' should read 'u = xi+eta+z' (required for (21) to hold and for (sqrt tu)=(r)).
First line '(sqrt x)+(sqrt xi)+(sqrt p)' etc. likely '(sqrt x)+(sqrt xi)+(p)' (characteristic p, not a radical); reading uncertain.
Line 2 garbled; probably '...und es kann kein Ausdruck aus dem selben ... in keiner der drei Gruppen ... vorkommen' (sense: none of the 16 can occur in the three groups r, q, p).
'(20) ... welche sich leicht aus (16) ergiebt' – the correction from (9.) to (16) is right.
